body: The spec's measurement logic has a near-tautology and a mislabeled design. (1) FR-008/SC-006 validate 'foresight' by measuring cosine similarity between the Low-Rank RL updates and the OPD subspace — but the Low-Rank RL updates are projected onto that subspace by construction (US-2: 'ensuring the update vector lies entirely within the span of the top-k vectors'). Early alignment with OPD is guaranteed by the intervention, not evidence that foresight was induced; the only non-circular outcome measures are the convergence-speed comparisons (FR-004/SC-001). (2) FR-005's 'optimal solution' proxy — the final accumulated update of the unconstrained PPO baseline — is arbitrary: there is no reason the standard PPO endpoint defines an optimal direction, so SC-002 measures similarity to a baseline, not to optimality; the spec itself concedes this is a proxy of convenience. (3) The 'observational data... without random assignment' framing in the assumptions is incorrect for this design: the projection IS randomly assignable across runs (via seeds), so the experiment is interventional and causal language would be licensed, provided seeds and hyperparameters are held fixed across variants. (4) FR-006/SC-003 propose a Wilcoxon test on 'three independent runs per variant' — three paired observations cannot support a p < 0.05 conclusion in any meaningful sense; the power analysis is deferred to post-hoc, after the design is frozen. (5) FR-007 cites 'US-4', which does not exist in the spec. (6) The 80%-explained-variance criterion for k (US-1, scenario 2) conflicts with the flat-spectrum edge case and the fixed default k=10; the deferred thresholds leave the geometric constraint — the core independent variable — undefined. (7) Feasibility: three variants × 3 seeds = 9 training runs of a 300M model on CPU within 6 hours total (FR-007, SC-005) is not established anywhere in the artifact; no per-run time budget is given. Also note the model-size assumption contains a literal placeholder ('A M parameter model').
